newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK's Daily Mail lifts H1 profits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK's Daily Mail lifts H1 profits.

text.p: Strong sales from its national titles helped British newspaper publisher Daily Mail and General Trust Plc to increase underlying half year profits by 27 percent, the company said on Thursday.

The group, which publishes the mid-market Daily Mail and Mail on Sunday national newspapers, reported pre-tax profit excluding exceptional items of 46.9 million pounds ($76.6 million) in the six months to March 30, up from 36.9 million.

"Trading conditions in the UK, still the predominant market for the group, remain positive. In these circumstances, the group expects to produce a satisfactory result at the full year," the company said in a statement.
The first half figures were towards the bottom end of share analysts' forecasts. Daily Mail shares remained unchanged at 1762.5 pence a share on the London Stock Exchange.

Analyst Anthony de Larrinaga of broker Panmure Gordon noted pre-Christmas weakness in advertising markets and said this may lead to some trimming of full-year forecasts. The consensus estimate for the year is for pre-tax profit of around 125 million pounds.

He added there was a fear the Labour government could extend Value Added Tax to newspapers in its first budget on July 2. He said Chancellor (Finance Minister) Gordon Brown might seek to introduce a rate of eight percent to bring Britain into line with its European partners.
However, another analyst pointed out VAT would be hard to implement as hundreds of local newspapers in Britain are distributed as "freesheets", carrying no cover price.

The group's flagship Daily Mail newspaper has consolidated its grip on the mid-market sector of the national newspaper business over the past two years. It has boosted sales since Rupert Murdoch's News International closed Today in 1995. The Daily Mail now sells some 2.1 million copies daily, over 900,000 ahead of its mid-market rival The Express.
The group said its newspaper operations, national and local, had benefited from a 15 percent fall in the cost of newsprint -- the raw material for newspapers.
The group reported a 12.4 million pound one-off profit on the sale of its stake in regional broadcaster Westcountry Television to Carlton Communications last December.

The interim dividend was lifted from 4.6 pence to 7.0 pence per share, the size of the rise reflecting an attempt to increase the proportion of the full-year total paid at this stage.($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
